}

function parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, runs, { legacyOffset = false } = {}) {
  const stdoutRe = /^\s*<!--\s*stdout from (codex\s+)?run (\d+)\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})[^>]*-->([\s\S]*?)(?=^\s*<!--\s*stdout from (?:codex\s+)?run \d|^\s*## Run \d|$(?![\s\S]))/gm
  let m
  while ((m = stdoutRe.exec(content)) !== null) {
    const [, codexMarker, slotStr, date, body] = m
    const failed = body.includes('[run failed')
    const boldRun = body.match(/\*\*Run (\d+)\s*(?:[—-]\s*([\w ]+?)\s*[—-]|\s*[—-]\s*done)/)
    const num = boldRun ? parseInt(boldRun[1]) : parseInt(slotStr) + (!codexMarker && legacyOffset ? 1 : 0)
    if (!num) continue

    const rawType = boldRun?.[2]?.trim().toUpperCase() || ''
    const type = failed ? 'FAILED' : ['MUTATE','RESEARCH','CREATE','RUN'].find(t => rawType.includes(t)) || rawType || 'RUN'
    const lines = body.split('\n').map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean)
    const failureLine = lines.find(l => l.startsWith('[run failed'))
    const detailLine = lines.find(l =>
      !l.startsWith('[run failed') &&
      !l.startsWith('**Run') &&
      !l.startsWith('---') &&
      !l.startsWith('```')
    )
    const summary = failed
      ? [failureLine, detailLine].filter(Boolean).join(' ')
      : detailLine || ''

    const formal = runs.find(r => r.num === num && r._source === 'formal')
    if (formal && !failed) continue

    const run = {
      num,
      date,
      type,
      'What I changed': summary || 'stdout captured with no summary',
      _order: m.index,
      _source: 'stdout',
    }
    run.signature = runSignature(run)
    runs.push(run)
  }
}

function parseFormalRunBlocks(content) {
  const runs = []
  const sections = content.split(/(?=^## Run \d)/m).filter(s => s.trimStart().startsWith('## Run'))
  let searchFrom = 0
  for (const block of sections) {
    const order = content.indexOf(block, searchFrom)
    if (order >= 0) searchFrom = order + block.length
    const lines = block.split('\n')
    const header = lines[0].replace('## Run ', '').trim()
    const parts = header.split(/\s+[—-]\s+/).map(s => s.trim())
    const [num, date, type] = parts
    const fields = {}
    for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
      if (line.startsWith('<!--')) break
      const m = line.match(/^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.+)/)
      if (m) fields[m[1]] = m[2]
    }
    const n = parseInt(num) || 0
    if (n) {
      const run = { num: n, date, type, ...fields, _order: order >= 0 ? order : runs.length, _source: 'formal' }
      run.signature = runSignature(run)
      runs.push(run)
    }
  }
  return runs
}

function parseRunsFromLog(content, options = {}) {
  const runs = parseFormalRunBlocks(content)
  parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, runs, options)
  return runs
    .sort((a, b) => (a._order ?? 0) - (b._order ?? 0))
    .map((run, _, sortedRuns) => {
      const key = `${run.num ?? ''}|${run.date ?? ''}`
      const attemptTotal = sortedRuns.filter(r => `${r.num ?? ''}|${r.date ?? ''}` === key).length
      if (attemptTotal <= 1) return run
      const attempt = sortedRuns
        .slice(0, sortedRuns.indexOf(run) + 1)
        .filter(r => `${r.num ?? ''}|${r.date ?? ''}` === key).length
      run._attemptKey = key
      run.attempt = attempt
      run.attemptTotal = attemptTotal
      run.signature = `${run.signature}|attempt:${attempt}/${attemptTotal}`
      return run

+function parseFormalRunBlocks(content) {

+  let searchFrom = 0
+  for (const block of sections) {
+    const order = content.indexOf(block, searchFrom)
+    if (order >= 0) searchFrom = order + block.length
+    const lines = block.split('\n')
+    const header = lines[0].replace('## Run ', '').trim()
+    const parts = header.split(/\s+[—-]\s+/).map(s => s.trim())
+    const [num, date, type] = parts
+    const fields = {}
+    for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
+      if (line.startsWith('<!--')) break
+      const m = line.match(/^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.+)/)
+      if (m) fields[m[1]] = m[2]
+    }
+    const n = parseInt(num) || 0

+  }

+function annotateRunAttempts(runs) {
+  const totals = new Map()
+  for (const run of runs) {

+    totals.set(key, (totals.get(key) ?? 0) + 1)

+
+  const seen = new Map()
+  return runs.map(run => {
+    const key = `${run.num ?? ''}|${run.date ?? ''}`
+    const attemptTotal = totals.get(key) ?? 1
+    if (attemptTotal <= 1) return run

+    const attempt = (seen.get(key) ?? 0) + 1
+    seen.set(key, attempt)
+    run._attemptKey = key
+    run.attempt = attempt
+    run.attemptTotal = attemptTotal
+    run.signature = `${run.signature}|attempt:${attempt}/${attemptTotal}`
+    return run
+  })

+## Run 91 — 2026-07-03 — MUTATE
+
+**What I changed:** Added duplicate-attempt metadata to parsed runs and rendered attempt suffixes plus `FAILED` styling in the host and incubator timelines.
+**Why:** The seed called for failed stdout-only runs to be visible, but repeated same-number failures still looked like the same event in history.
+**What improved:** Failed retries now keep stable signatures, show as distinct timeline entries, and display `attempt n/total` when the log contains repeated run numbers.
+**What broke:** The underlying log still allows repeated run numbers; this only makes the ambiguity visible instead of preventing it.
+**Next move:** Add a runner preflight status row that checks missing binaries like `codex` before scheduled incubator runs fire.

+## Run 91 — 2026-07-03 — MUTATE
+
+**What I changed:** Added duplicate-attempt metadata to parsed runs and rendered attempt suffixes plus `FAILED` styling in the host and incubator timelines.
+**Why:** The seed called for failed stdout-only runs to be visible, but repeated same-number failures still looked like the same event in history.
+**What improved:** Failed retries now keep stable signatures, show as distinct timeline entries, and display `attempt n/total` when the log contains repeated run numbers.
+**What broke:** The underlying log still allows repeated run numbers; this only makes the ambiguity visible instead of preventing it.
+**Next move:** Add a runner preflight status row that checks missing binaries like `codex` before scheduled incubator runs fire.

- Parser check confirmed all three `codex exited 127` run 88 blocks now appear separately as `FAILED #88` with the shell error.

I did not start a new dev server because port `8089` is already occupied by an existing `node` process.

## Run 91 — 2026-07-03 — MUTATE

**What I changed:** Added duplicate-attempt metadata to parsed runs and rendered attempt suffixes plus `FAILED` styling in the host and incubator timelines.
**Why:** The seed called for failed stdout-only runs to be visible, but repeated same-number failures still looked like the same event in history.
**What improved:** Failed retries now keep stable signatures, show as distinct timeline entries, and display `attempt n/total` when the log contains repeated run numbers.
**What broke:** The underlying log still allows repeated run numbers; this only makes the ambiguity visible instead of preventing it.
**Next move:** Add a runner preflight status row that checks missing binaries like `codex` before scheduled incubator runs fire.

+

## Run 92 — 2026-07-03 — RESEARCH

**What I investigated:** Pi Pulse incubator-host reliability around run parsing, API JSON boundaries, per-incubator local Ollama/Qwen feedback, and runner preflight behavior.
**Key finding:** `parseStdoutRunBlocks()` treats any stdout body containing `[run failed` as failed; live `/api/runs` therefore reports a successful Codex stdout block for run 89 as `FAILED` because the transcript/log text contains that marker elsewhere.
**Implication:** The next build run should tighten failure classification before adding more history UI, otherwise the timeline can confidently display false failures.
**Suggested next move:** Change stdout failure detection to anchor on the first meaningful stdout line, then verify `/api/runs` no longer reports `FAILED #89` for `[run completed successfully...]` while still preserving real `codex exited 127` failures.

import express from 'express'
import fs from 'fs'
import os from 'os'
import { spawn, execSync } from 'child_process'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'url'
import { dirname, join } from 'path'

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const app = express()
const PORT = 8089
const RUN_LOG_PATH = '/home/admin/lab/RUN_LOG.md'

// CPU usage calculation (requires two samples)
let prevCpuTimes = null

// Network I/O — requires two samples to compute bytes/sec rate
let prevNetSample = null

// Cached last stats payload — used by pushDaySnapshot to avoid double-sampling
let lastStatsPayload = null

// Active run tracking — cleared after process exits and status is read
let activeRun = null // { pid, startTime }

const LAB_RUNNERS = {
  claude: {
    script: '/home/admin/run-lab.sh',
    args: [],
  },
  codex: {
    script: '/home/admin/lab/scripts/run-codex-incubator.sh',
    args: ['/home/admin/lab/projects/pi-pulse/status.json'],
  },
}
const LAB_SCHEDULE_PATH = '/home/admin/lab/projects/pi-pulse/schedule.json'
let labScheduleState = { enabled: false, intervalHours: 2, runner: 'claude', nextRunAt: null, lastScheduledRun: null, autoRunsSinceHuman: 0 }

try {
  const raw = fs.readFileSync(LAB_SCHEDULE_PATH, 'utf8')
  const loaded = JSON.parse(raw)
  labScheduleState = { ...labScheduleState, ...loaded }
  if (labScheduleState.enabled && labScheduleState.nextRunAt && labScheduleState.nextRunAt < Date.now()) {
    labScheduleState.nextRunAt = Date.now() + labScheduleState.intervalHours * 60 * 60 * 1000
  }
} catch { /* no host lab schedule yet */ }

function saveLabSchedule() {
  try { fs.writeFileSync(LAB_SCHEDULE_PATH, JSON.stringify(labScheduleState, null, 2) + '\n') } catch {}
}

function activeRunAlive() {
  if (!activeRun) return false
  try {
    process.kill(activeRun.pid, 0)
    return true
  } catch {
    activeRun = null
    return false
  }
}

function normalizeLabRunner(runner) {
  return Object.hasOwn(LAB_RUNNERS, runner) ? runner : 'claude'
}

function startLabRun(runner = labScheduleState.runner) {
  const selected = normalizeLabRunner(runner)
  const cfg = LAB_RUNNERS[selected]
  if (!fs.existsSync(cfg.script)) return null
  const child = spawn('bash', [cfg.script, ...cfg.args], {
    cwd: '/home/admin/lab',
    detached: true,
    stdio: 'ignore',
  })
  child.unref()
  activeRun = { pid: child.pid, startTime: Date.now(), runner: selected }
  return child
}

function readCpuTimes() {
  try {
    const stat = fs.readFileSync('/proc/stat', 'utf8')
    const line = stat.split('\n')[0]
    const parts = line.replace('cpu  ', '').trim().split(/\s+/).map(Number)
    const [user, nice, system, idle, iowait, irq, softirq, steal] = parts
    const total = user + nice + system + idle + (iowait || 0) + (irq || 0) + (softirq || 0) + (steal || 0)
    return { total, idle: idle + (iowait || 0) }
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

function getCpuUsage() {
  const curr = readCpuTimes()
  if (!curr || !prevCpuTimes) {
    prevCpuTimes = curr
    return 0
  }
  const totalDiff = curr.total - prevCpuTimes.total
  const idleDiff = curr.idle - prevCpuTimes.idle
  prevCpuTimes = curr
  if (totalDiff === 0) return 0
  return Math.round(((totalDiff - idleDiff) / totalDiff) * 100)
}

function getMemInfo() {
  try {
    const mem = fs.readFileSync('/proc/meminfo', 'utf8')
    const parse = (key) => {
      const match = mem.match(new RegExp(`${key}:\\s+(\\d+)`))
      return match ? parseInt(match[1]) * 1024 : 0
    }
    const total = parse('MemTotal')
    const free = parse('MemFree')
    const buffers = parse('Buffers')
    const cached = parse('Cached')
    const used = total - free - buffers - cached
    return {
      total,
      used,
      free: total - used,
      percent: Math.round((used / total) * 100),
    }
  } catch {
    const total = os.totalmem()
    const free = os.freemem()
    return { total, used: total - free, free, percent: Math.round(((total - free) / total) * 100) }
  }
}

function getTemperature() {
  const paths = [
    '/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp',
    '/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon0/temp1_input',
  ]
  for (const p of paths) {
    try {
      const raw = fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').trim()
      const temp = parseInt(raw)
      return temp > 1000 ? temp / 1000 : temp
    } catch { /* continue */ }
  }
  return null
}

function getUptime() {
  try {
    const raw = fs.readFileSync('/proc/uptime', 'utf8')
    return Math.floor(parseFloat(raw.split(' ')[0]))
  } catch {
    return os.uptime()
  }
}

function getLoadAvg() {
  try {
    const raw = fs.readFileSync('/proc/loadavg', 'utf8')
    const parts = raw.trim().split(' ')
    return [parseFloat(parts[0]), parseFloat(parts[1]), parseFloat(parts[2])]
  } catch {
    return os.loadavg()
  }
}

function formatUptime(seconds) {
  const d = Math.floor(seconds / 86400)
  const h = Math.floor((seconds % 86400) / 3600)
  const m = Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60)
  if (d > 0) return `${d}d ${h}h`
  if (h > 0) return `${h}h ${m}m`
  return `${m}m`
}

function getDiskInfo() {
  try {
    const out = execSync('df -B1 / 2>/dev/null', { timeout: 3000 }).toString().trim()
    const lines = out.split('\n')
    if (lines.length < 2) return null
    const parts = lines[1].trim().split(/\s+/)
    const total = parseInt(parts[1])
    const used = parseInt(parts[2])
    const pct = parseInt(parts[4])
    return {
      totalGB: (total / 1e9).toFixed(1),
      usedGB: (used / 1e9).toFixed(1),
      percent: isNaN(pct) ? 0 : pct,
    }
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

function getNetworkRate() {
  try {
    const raw = fs.readFileSync('/proc/net/dev', 'utf8')
    const lines = raw.trim().split('\n').slice(2)
    const SKIP = /^(lo|docker|veth|br-|vmnet|virbr)/
    let best = null
    for (const line of lines) {
      const colonIdx = line.indexOf(':')
      if (colonIdx < 0) continue
      const iface = line.slice(0, colonIdx).trim()
      if (SKIP.test(iface)) continue
      const fields = line.slice(colonIdx + 1).trim().split(/\s+/).map(Number)
      const rx = fields[0]  // receive bytes
      const tx = fields[8]  // transmit bytes
      if (!best || rx > best.rx) best = { iface, rx, tx, ts: Date.now() }
    }
    if (!best) return { rx: 0, tx: 0, iface: 'unknown' }
    if (!prevNetSample || best.iface !== prevNetSample.iface) {
      prevNetSample = best
      return { rx: 0, tx: 0, iface: best.iface }
    }
    const dt = (best.ts - prevNetSample.ts) / 1000
    const rx = dt > 0 ? Math.max(0, Math.round((best.rx - prevNetSample.rx) / dt)) : 0
    const tx = dt > 0 ? Math.max(0, Math.round((best.tx - prevNetSample.tx) / dt)) : 0
    prevNetSample = best
    return { rx, tx, iface: best.iface }
  } catch {
    return { rx: 0, tx: 0, iface: 'unknown' }
  }
}

// ─── Project status sync ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const PROJECT_STATUS_PATH = '/home/admin/lab/projects/pi-pulse/status.json'

    const runs = parseRunsFromLog(content, { legacyOffset: true })
    const latest = runs[runs.length - 1] ?? null

    let current = {}

    const updated = {
      ...current,
      runCount: latest?.num ?? current.runCount ?? 0,
      lastRun: latest?.date ?? current.lastRun,
      lastRunType: latest?.type ?? current.lastRunType,
      syncedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    }

    fs.writeFileSync(PROJECT_STATUS_PATH, JSON.stringify(updated, null, 2) + '\n')

    // Keep project-level seed.md in sync with the daily seed
    try {
      const seedContent = fs.readFileSync('/home/admin/lab/DAILY_SEED.md', 'utf8')
      fs.writeFileSync('/home/admin/lab/projects/pi-pulse/seed.md', seedContent)
    } catch { /* non-fatal */ }
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('[pi-pulse] status sync error:', err.message)
  }
}

// Prime the CPU baseline
readCpuTimes()

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { useSystemStats } from './hooks/useSystemStats.js'
import { NavShell } from './components/NavShell.jsx'
import { PulsePanel } from './components/PulsePanel.jsx'
import { ProjectPanel } from './components/ProjectPanel.jsx'
import { LabPanel } from './components/LabPanel.jsx'

// Ambient color thresholds — shifts the whole UI accent as load rises
const COOL   = { accent: '#22d3ee', dim: 'rgba(34,211,238,0.12)',  glow: 'rgba(34,211,238,0.35)'  }
const WARM   = { accent: '#fb923c', dim: 'rgba(251,146,60,0.12)',  glow: 'rgba(251,146,60,0.35)'  }
const HOT    = { accent: '#f87171', dim: 'rgba(248,113,113,0.12)', glow: 'rgba(248,113,113,0.35)' }

function applyAccent({ accent, dim, glow }) {
  const r = document.documentElement.style
  r.setProperty('--accent', accent)
  r.setProperty('--accent-dim', dim)
  r.setProperty('--accent-glow', glow)
}

// Circadian ambient — bloom opacity and vertical position follow the time of day.
// Night: dim and receded. Dawn: rising. Day: full presence. Dusk: fading.
function useCircadian() {
  const compute = () => {
    const h = new Date().getHours() + new Date().getMinutes() / 60
    if (h >= 22 || h < 5) return { opacity: 0.07, top: '-6vh' }   // deep night — receded
    if (h < 8) {                                                    // dawn — rising
      const p = (h - 5) / 3
      return { opacity: 0.07 + p * 0.09, top: `${(-6 + p * 6).toFixed(1)}vh` }
    }
    if (h < 18) return { opacity: 0.16, top: '0vh' }               // day — full presence
    const p = (h - 18) / 4                                         // dusk — fading
    return { opacity: 0.16 - p * 0.09, top: `${(-p * 6).toFixed(1)}vh` }
  }
  const [state, setState] = useState(compute)
  useEffect(() => {
    const id = setInterval(() => setState(compute()), 60_000)
    return () => clearInterval(id)
  }, [])
  return state
}

function fmtBytes(b) {
  if (b == null) return '—'
  if (b < 1024) return `${b} B/s`
  if (b < 1024 * 1024) return `${(b / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB/s`
  return `${(b / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1)} MB/s`
}

function SystemStrip({ stats, latestTemp, connected }) {
  const disk = stats?.disk?.percent ?? null
  const memory = stats?.memory?.percent ?? null
  const cpu = stats?.cpu ?? null
  const hot = latestTemp > 70 || cpu > 85
  const diskHigh = disk != null && disk > 88
  const status = hot ? 'hot' : diskHigh ? 'disk pressure' : connected ? 'safe' : 'offline'
  const statusColor = hot ? '#f87171' : diskHigh ? '#fb923c' : connected ? '#22c55e' : '#64748b'

  const metric = (label, value, color = 'rgba(226,232,240,0.72)') => (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 2, minWidth: 64 }}>
      <span style={{ fontSize: '0.52rem', fontFamily: 'monospace', textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.12em', color: 'rgba(71,85,105,0.62)' }}>
        {label}
      </span>
      <strong style={{ fontSize: '0.78rem', fontFamily: 'monospace', color, fontWeight: 650, lineHeight: 1 }}>
        {value}
      </strong>
    </div>
  )

  return (
    <div
      className="panel"
      style={{
        padding: '10px 16px',
        display: 'flex',
        flexWrap: 'wrap',
        gap: 12,
        alignItems: 'center',
      }}
    >
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 9, minWidth: 140, flex: '1 1 160px' }}>
        <span style={{
          width: 8,
          height: 8,
          borderRadius: '50%',
          background: statusColor,
          boxShadow: `0 0 10px ${statusColor}66`,
          flexShrink: 0,
        }} />
        <div style={{ minWidth: 0 }}>
          <div style={{ fontSize: '0.58rem', fontFamily: 'monospace', textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.14em', color: statusColor }}>
            {status}
          </div>
          <div style={{ marginTop: 2, fontSize: '0.62rem', color: 'rgba(148,163,184,0.56)', overflow: 'hidden', textOverflow: 'ellipsis', whiteSpace: 'nowrap' }}>
            {stats?.hostname ?? 'pi'} · {stats?.uptimeFormatted ?? '—'}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      {metric('cpu', cpu == null ? '—' : `${cpu}%`, cpu > 65 ? '#fb923c' : undefined)}
      {metric('temp', latestTemp == null ? '—' : `${latestTemp.toFixed(1)}°`, latestTemp > 60 ? '#fb923c' : undefined)}
      {metric('mem', memory == null ? '—' : `${memory}%`)}
      {metric('disk', disk == null ? '—' : `${disk}%`, diskHigh ? '#fb923c' : undefined)}
      {metric('net ↓', fmtBytes(stats?.net?.rx), '#22d3ee')}
      {metric('net ↑', fmtBytes(stats?.net?.tx), '#a78bfa')}
    </div>
  )
}

function CollapsiblePulse({ stats, history, tempHistory, netRxHistory, netTxHistory }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

  return (
    <section className="panel" style={{ padding: 0, overflow: 'hidden' }}>
      <button
        onClick={() => setOpen(o => !o)}
        style={{
          width: '100%',
          border: 'none',
          background: 'transparent',
          padding: '12px 18px',
          display: 'flex',
          alignItems: 'center',
          gap: 10,
          cursor: 'pointer',
          color: 'inherit',
          textAlign: 'left',
        }}
      >
        <span style={{
          width: 7,
          height: 7,
          borderRadius: '50%',
          background: 'var(--accent)',
          boxShadow: '0 0 10px var(--accent-glow)',
          flexShrink: 0,
        }} />
        <div style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>
          <div style={{ fontSize: '0.58rem', fontFamily: 'monospace', textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.14em', color: 'var(--muted)' }}>
            System Pulse
          </div>
          <div style={{ marginTop: 3, fontSize: '0.72rem', color: 'rgba(148,163,184,0.58)' }}>
            Full telemetry chamber, expanded only when you need the diagnostics.
          </div>
        </div>
        <span style={{ fontSize: '0.64rem', fontFamily: 'monospace', color: 'rgba(71,85,105,0.55)', textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.08em' }}>
          {open ? 'hide' : 'open'}
        </span>
      </button>
      {open && (
        <div style={{ borderTop: '1px solid var(--border)', padding: 16 }}>
          <PulsePanel stats={stats} history={history} tempHistory={tempHistory} netRxHistory={netRxHistory} netTxHistory={netTxHistory} />
        </div>
      )}
    </section>
  )
}

function summarizeRun(run) {
  return run['Failure'] || run['Error'] || run['Goal'] || run['Done'] ||
    run['What I investigated'] || run['Investigated'] || run['What I built'] ||
    run['What I changed'] || run['What improved'] || run['What I found'] ||
    run['Key finding'] || run['Suggested next move'] || ''
}

function publicRun(run) {
  const { _order, _source, _attemptKey, ...rest } = run
  return rest
}

function runSignature(run) {
  return [
    run._source ?? 'run',
    run._order ?? 0,
    run.num ?? '',
    run.date ?? '',
    run.type ?? '',
    summarizeRun(run),
  ].join('|')
}

function parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, runs, { legacyOffset = false } = {}) {
  const stdoutRe = /^\s*<!--\s*stdout from (codex\s+)?run (\d+)\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})[^>]*-->([\s\S]*?)(?=^\s*<!--\s*stdout from (?:codex\s+)?run \d|^\s*## Run \d|$(?![\s\S]))/gm
  let m
  while ((m = stdoutRe.exec(content)) !== null) {
    const [, codexMarker, slotStr, date, body] = m
    const failed = body.includes('[run failed')
    const boldRun = body.match(/\*\*Run (\d+)\s*(?:[—-]\s*([\w ]+?)\s*[—-]|\s*[—-]\s*done)/)
    const num = boldRun ? parseInt(boldRun[1]) : parseInt(slotStr) + (!codexMarker && legacyOffset ? 1 : 0)
    if (!num) continue

    const rawType = boldRun?.[2]?.trim().toUpperCase() || ''
    const type = failed ? 'FAILED' : ['MUTATE','RESEARCH','CREATE','RUN'].find(t => rawType.includes(t)) || rawType || 'RUN'
    const lines = body.split('\n').map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean)
    const failureLine = lines.find(l => l.startsWith('[run failed'))
    const detailLine = lines.find(l =>
      !l.startsWith('[run failed') &&
      !l.startsWith('**Run') &&
      !l.startsWith('---') &&
      !l.startsWith('```')
    )
    const summary = failed
      ? [failureLine, detailLine].filter(Boolean).join(' ')
      : detailLine || ''

    const formal = runs.find(r => r.num === num && r._source === 'formal')
    if (formal && !failed) continue

    const run = {
      num,
      date,
      type,
      'What I changed': summary || 'stdout captured with no summary',
      _order: m.index,
      _source: 'stdout',
    }
    run.signature = runSignature(run)
    runs.push(run)
  }
}

function parseFormalRunBlocks(content) {
  const runs = []
  const sections = content.split(/(?=^## Run \d)/m).filter(s => s.trimStart().startsWith('## Run'))
  let searchFrom = 0
  for (const block of sections) {
    const order = content.indexOf(block, searchFrom)
    if (order >= 0) searchFrom = order + block.length
    const lines = block.split('\n')
    const header = lines[0].replace('## Run ', '').trim()
    const parts = header.split(/\s+[—-]\s+/).map(s => s.trim())
    const [num, date, type] = parts
    const fields = {}
    for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
      if (line.startsWith('<!--')) break
      const m = line.match(/^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.+)/)
      if (m) fields[m[1]] = m[2]
    }
    const n = parseInt(num) || 0
    if (n) {
      const run = { num: n, date, type, ...fields, _order: order >= 0 ? order : runs.length, _source: 'formal' }
      run.signature = runSignature(run)
      runs.push(run)
    }
  }
  return runs
}

function annotateRunAttempts(runs) {
  const totals = new Map()
  for (const run of runs) {
    const key = `${run.num ?? ''}|${run.date ?? ''}`
    totals.set(key, (totals.get(key) ?? 0) + 1)
  }

  const seen = new Map()
  return runs.map(run => {
    const key = `${run.num ?? ''}|${run.date ?? ''}`
    const attemptTotal = totals.get(key) ?? 1
    if (attemptTotal <= 1) return run

    const attempt = (seen.get(key) ?? 0) + 1
    seen.set(key, attempt)
    run._attemptKey = key
    run.attempt = attempt
    run.attemptTotal = attemptTotal
    run.signature = `${run.signature}|attempt:${attempt}/${attemptTotal}`
    return run
  })
}

function parseRunsFromLog(content, options = {}) {
  const runs = parseFormalRunBlocks(content)
  parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, runs, options)
  const sortedRuns = runs.sort((a, b) => (a._order ?? 0) - (b._order ?? 0))
  return annotateRunAttempts(sortedRuns).map(publicRun)
}

    try { res.write(':heartbeat\n\n') } catch { clearInterval(heartbeat) }
  }, 25000)
  req.on('close', () => {
    runClients.delete(res)
    clearInterval(heartbeat)
  })
})

import { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
import { motion } from 'framer-motion'

const KEY_MAP = {
  DIRECTION: ['direction', 'dir', 'duration', 'heading'],
  STRONGEST: ['strongest', 'strong', 'best', 'winning'],
  WEAKEST:   ['weakest', 'weak', 'worst', 'problem'],
  DRIFT:     ['drift', 'drifting'],
  NEXT:      ['next', 'mutate', 'suggested', 'suggestion', 'move', 'priority'],
}

function parseAnalysis(text) {
  const fields = {}
  const cleaned = text.replace(/\*\*/g, '').replace(/\r/g, '')
  const re = /([A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*):\s*\n?([\s\S]*?)(?=\n[A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*:|$)/g
  let m
  while ((m = re.exec(cleaned)) !== null) {
    const rawKey = m[1].trim().toLowerCase()
    const value = m[2].trim().replace(/\n+/g, ' ')
    if (!value) continue
    for (const [canonical, aliases] of Object.entries(KEY_MAP)) {
      if (aliases.some(a => rawKey.includes(a))) {
        fields[canonical] = value
        break
      }
    }
  }
  return fields
}

  const [labLaunching, setLabLaunching] = useState(false)

  const latestRunSignature = (runs) => {
    const latest = runs.at(-1)
    if (!latest) return 'empty'
    const what = latest['Failure'] || latest['Error'] || latest['Goal'] || latest['Done'] || latest['What I investigated'] || latest['Investigated'] || latest['What I built'] || latest['What I changed'] || latest['What improved'] || latest['What I found'] || latest['Key finding'] || latest['Suggested next move'] || ''
    return latest.signature || `${latest.num ?? ''}|${latest.date ?? ''}|${latest.type ?? ''}|${what}|${runs.length}`
  }

  const noteLatestRun = (id, runs) => {
    const signature = latestRunSignature(runs)
    const prev = runSignatureBySlotRef.current[id]
    if (prev != null && signature !== prev) {
      setAiTriggersBySlot(current => ({ ...current, [id]: (current[id] || 0) + 1 }))
    }
    runSignatureBySlotRef.current[id] = signature
  }

  }

const AI_FIELD_META = [
  { key: 'DIRECTION', label: 'Direction', color: 'var(--accent)' },
  { key: 'STRONGEST', label: 'Strongest', color: '#22c55e' },
  { key: 'WEAKEST',   label: 'Weakest',   color: '#f97316' },
  { key: 'DRIFT',     label: 'Drift',     color: '#a78bfa' },
  { key: 'NEXT',      label: 'Next',      color: '#38bdf8' },
]

function parseAnalysis(text) {
  const fields = {}
  const re = /([A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*):\s*\n?([\s\S]*?)(?=\n[A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*:|$)/g
  let m
  while ((m = re.exec(text.replace(/\*\*/g, '').replace(/\r/g, ''))) !== null) {
    const key = m[1].trim().toUpperCase()
    const val = m[2].trim().replace(/\n+/g, ' ')
    if (val && AI_FIELD_META.some(f => f.key === key)) fields[key] = val
  }
  return fields
}

      prevTriggerBySlotRef.current[slotId] = autoTrigger

      setError(err.message)
    } finally {
      setLoading(false)
    }

const LOG_TYPE_COLOR = { CREATE: '#22d3ee', MUTATE: '#a78bfa', RESEARCH: '#34d399', HARVEST: '#fbbf24' }
const LOG_FIELD_COLOR = {
  'What I changed': '#e2e8f0', 'What I built': '#e2e8f0', 'What I investigated': '#e2e8f0',

  'Next move': '#38bdf8', 'Suggested next move': '#38bdf8', 'Implication': '#38bdf8',
}

function parseRunLog(content) {
  const blocks = content.split(/(?=^## Run \d)/m).filter(s => s.trimStart().startsWith('## Run'))
  return blocks.map(block => {
    // Strip stdout comment dumps
    const clean = block.replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, '').replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n').trim()
    const lines = clean.split('\n')
    const header = lines[0].replace('## Run ', '')
    const parts = header.split(' — ').map(s => s.trim())
    const num = parts[0], date = parts[1], type = parts[2]
    const fields = []
    for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
      const m = line.match(/^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.+)/)
      if (m) fields.push({ label: m[1], value: m[2] })
    }
    return { num, date, type, fields }
  }).reverse()
}

function LogModal({ content, onClose }) {
  const runs = useMemo(() => parseRunLog(content), [content])

RUN_COUNT=$(node -e "console.log(Math.max(Number(process.argv[1] || 0), Number(process.argv[2] || 0)))" "${LAST_RUN:-0}" "$STATUS_RUN_COUNT")

runs = [s.strip() for s in sections if s.strip().startswith("## Run")]
recent = runs[-4:] if len(runs) >= 4 else runs

with open(recent_path, 'w') as f:
    f.write("# Recent Runs\n\n")

CODEX_EXIT=0
CODEX_ARGS=(exec -C "$PROJECT_DIR" --add-dir "$LAB_DIR" --color never)
if [ -n "$CODEX_BYPASS" ]; then

else

if [ -n "$CODEX_MODEL" ]; then

$OUTPUT"

const [path, runType, today, exitCode, runNumber] = process.argv.slice(2)
try {
  const status = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
  status.runner = status.runner || 'codex'
  status.runCount = Number(runNumber)
  status.lastRun = today
  status.lastRunType = runType.toUpperCase()
  status.lastRunStatus = exitCode === '0' ? 'ok' : 'failed'
  fs.writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(status, null, 2) + '\n')
} catch (err) {
  console.error(`[codex-incubator] warning: could not update status: ${err.message}`)
}
NODEEOF

#!/bin/bash
# run-lab.sh — seed -> drift -> report loop
# Runs Claude Code headless in feral lab mode.
# Triggered by systemd timer or manually.

set -euo pipefail

# Use OAuth (claude.ai subscription) — never API key
unset CLAUDECODE 2>/dev/null || true
unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY 2>/dev/null || true
unset ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN 2>/dev/null || true

LAB_DIR=/home/admin/lab
LOG_FILE=$LAB_DIR/RUN_LOG.md
RECENT_FILE=$LAB_DIR/RECENT_RUNS.md
SEED_FILE=$LAB_DIR/DAILY_SEED.md
MEMPALACE=/home/admin/.local/bin/mempalace
TIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')
CLAUDE_MODEL=${CLAUDE_MODEL:-fable}

# Rotation: create -> mutate -> research -> mutate -> repeat
# Harvest is manual only: ./run-lab.sh harvest
RUN_TYPES=("create" "mutate" "research" "mutate")
# Derive from max existing run number, not header count.
# Handles duplicates (runs 6/9/59 have appeared twice) and gaps (12/24/33 missing)
# without collision on the next number.
LAST_RUN=$(grep -oE "^## Run [0-9]+" "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | sort -n | tail -1 || true)
RUN_COUNT=${LAST_RUN:-0}

if [[ "${1:-}" =~ ^(create|mutate|research|harvest)$ ]]; then
    RUN_TYPE="$1"
else
    RUN_TYPE="${RUN_TYPES[$((RUN_COUNT % ${#RUN_TYPES[@]}))]}"
fi

PROMPT_FILE=$LAB_DIR/prompts/$RUN_TYPE.md

echo "[run-lab] $TIMESTAMP — starting $RUN_TYPE run (#$((RUN_COUNT + 1)))"

# Generate lean MEMORY_BRIEF.md from MemPalace before loading the prompt
bash "$LAB_DIR/generate-brief.sh" "$RUN_TYPE" || echo "[run-lab] brief generation failed (non-fatal)"

# Regenerate RECENT_RUNS.md from the last 4 entries in RUN_LOG.md
# Handles both ## Run N headings and <!-- stdout from run N --> blocks
python3 - "$LOG_FILE" "$RECENT_FILE" << 'PYEOF'
import sys, re

log_path, recent_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

try:
    text = open(log_path).read()
except FileNotFoundError:
    text = ""

by_num = {}

# Format 1: formal ## Run N — DATE — TYPE sections
for m in re.finditer(r'^(## Run (\d+) — .+?)(?=^## Run \d|\Z)', text, re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL):
    num = int(m.group(2))
    # Trim at first stdout comment so we don't bloat with old stdout
    block = re.split(r'<!--\s*stdout from run', m.group(1))[0].strip()
    by_num[num] = block

# Format 2: <!-- stdout from run N DATE --> blocks
for m in re.finditer(r'<!--\s*stdout from run (\d+)\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})[^>]*-->([\s\S]*?)(?=<!--\s*stdout from run \d|\Z)', text):
    slot, date, body = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2), m.group(3).strip()
    if not body or '[run failed' in body:
        continue
    # Bold **Run N — TYPE** inside body names the actual run
    bm = re.search(r'\*\*Run (\d+)\s*(?:—\s*([\w ]+?)\s*—|—\s*done)', body)
    num = int(bm.group(1)) if bm else slot + 1
    raw_type = (bm.group(2) or '').strip().upper() if bm else ''
    run_type = next((t for t in ['MUTATE','RESEARCH','CREATE'] if t in raw_type), raw_type or 'RUN')
    if num not in by_num:
        # Trim body to first 60 lines to keep RECENT_RUNS concise
        trimmed = '\n'.join(body.splitlines()[:60])
        by_num[num] = f"## Run {num} — {date} — {run_type}\n\n{trimmed}"

runs = [by_num[k] for k in sorted(by_num)]
recent = runs[-4:] if len(runs) >= 4 else runs

with open(recent_path, 'w') as f:
    f.write("# Recent Runs\n\n")
    f.write("*Auto-generated. Last 4 runs. Full history in RUN_LOG.md.*\n\n---\n\n")
    f.write("\n\n---\n\n".join(recent) if recent else "*(no runs yet)*\n")
PYEOF

# Run Claude Code headless in the lab directory
cd "$LAB_DIR"
FULL_PROMPT=$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")
BUILD_MARKER=$(mktemp)
CLAUDE_EXIT=0
OUTPUT=$(claude \
    --print \
    --allowedTools "Read Write Edit Bash(npm*) Bash(npx*) Bash(cd*) Bash(cat*) Bash(ls*)" \
    --add-dir "$LAB_DIR" \
    --model "$CLAUDE_MODEL" \
    "$FULL_PROMPT" 2>&1) || CLAUDE_EXIT=$?

if [ "$CLAUDE_EXIT" -ne 0 ]; then
    OUTPUT="[run failed — claude exited $CLAUDE_EXIT]

$OUTPUT"
fi

echo "[run-lab] run complete, logging"

# Post-run build check — not a milestone gate, just "did it compile".
# Only fires when the run actually touched pi-pulse source; catches a run
# claiming success while leaving the UI broken (decisions.md: never deploy
# a failing build).
BUILD_NOTE=""
CHANGED=$(find "$LAB_DIR/src/pi-pulse/src" \
    "$LAB_DIR/src/pi-pulse/server.js" \
    "$LAB_DIR/src/pi-pulse/index.html" \
    "$LAB_DIR/src/pi-pulse/tailwind.config.js" \
    "$LAB_DIR/src/pi-pulse/postcss.config.js" \
    "$LAB_DIR/src/pi-pulse/vite.config.js" \
    -type f -newer "$BUILD_MARKER" -print -quit 2>/dev/null || true)
rm -f "$BUILD_MARKER"
if [ -n "$CHANGED" ]; then
    echo "[run-lab] pi-pulse source changed — verifying npm run build"
    if (cd "$LAB_DIR/src/pi-pulse" && npm run build > /dev/null 2>&1); then
        BUILD_NOTE="[build check] PASS — this run changed pi-pulse and npm run build succeeded"
    else
        BUILD_NOTE="[build check] FAIL — this run changed pi-pulse and npm run build FAILED; UI may be broken"
    fi
    echo "[run-lab] $BUILD_NOTE"
fi

# Claude should have written directly to RUN_LOG.md and ACTIVE_THREADS.md
# as instructed by the prompt. Append its stdout too as a fallback record.
{
    echo ""
    echo "<!-- stdout from run $((RUN_COUNT + 1)) $TIMESTAMP -->"
    echo "$OUTPUT"
    if [ -n "$BUILD_NOTE" ]; then
        echo ""
        echo "$BUILD_NOTE"
    fi
    echo ""
} >> "$LOG_FILE"

# Save run summary to structured memory and mine just the memory dir
bash "$LAB_DIR/save-run.sh" "$((RUN_COUNT + 1))" || echo "[run-lab] save-run failed (non-fatal)"

echo "[run-lab] done"

exec

 I did not start a new dev server because port `8089` is already occupied by an existing `node` process.
 
+## Run 91 — 2026-07-03 — MUTATE
+
+**What I changed:** Added duplicate-attempt metadata to parsed runs and rendered attempt suffixes plus `FAILED` styling in the host and incubator timelines.
+**Why:** The seed called for failed stdout-only runs to be visible, but repeated same-number failures still looked like the same event in history.
+**What improved:** Failed retries now keep stable signatures, show as distinct timeline entries, and display `attempt n/total` when the log contains repeated run numbers.
+**What broke:** The underlying log still allows repeated run numbers; this only makes the ambiguity visible instead of preventing it.
+**Next move:** Add a runner preflight status row that checks missing binaries like `codex` before scheduled incubator runs fire.

+function annotateRunAttempts(runs) {
+  const totals = new Map()
+  for (const run of runs) {
+    const key = `${run.num ?? ''}|${run.date ?? ''}`
+    totals.set(key, (totals.get(key) ?? 0) + 1)
+  }
+
+  const seen = new Map()
+  return runs.map(run => {
+    const key = `${run.num ?? ''}|${run.date ?? ''}`
+    const attemptTotal = totals.get(key) ?? 1
+    if (attemptTotal <= 1) return run
+
+    const attempt = (seen.get(key) ?? 0) + 1
+    seen.set(key, attempt)
+    run._attemptKey = key
+    run.attempt = attempt
+    run.attemptTotal = attemptTotal
+    run.signature = `${run.signature}|attempt:${attempt}/${attemptTotal}`
+    return run
+  })
+}
+

   const runs = parseFormalRunBlocks(content)
   parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, runs, options)

# Backlog

## ghost/whisper/oracle as incubated project
The quartet (src/ghost/) is dormant — 5 standalone JS files, ports 3032–3036. Per the seed, it must NOT be integrated into Pi Pulse's Pulse tab UI. The correct pattern: create `projects/ghost-trio/status.json` with repo/runLog/runScript fields, point `mounted.json` at it, restart pi-pulse. Then the quartet gets its own ProjectPanel slot and run history without touching the waveform layer. One status.json + one run script = fully mounted. This is the right way to continue the ghost/oracle work without violating the "no new instruments" rule.

## server.js: replace hardcoded 'race-whisperer-predict' fallback strings
`loadMountedProject()` in `server.js` has hardcoded fallback values (`name: 'race-whisperer-predict'`, `dir: '/home/admin/race-whisperer-predict'`, etc.) that fire when `mounted.json` is missing or malformed. The silent-catch was fixed on 2026-07-03 (now logs `console.error`), but the fallback still steers a broken config at race-whisperer. Better fallback: throw and let systemd surface it, OR fall back to a minimal safe stub that clearly identifies as a config-error state. Not urgent — the console.error already makes the failure visible.

## Surface auto-run staleness in ProjectPanel
`GET /api/child/schedule` now returns `autoRunsSinceHuman` — increments on every scheduled auto-fire, resets when a human triggers a run or edits the schedule. Surface it in ProjectPanel once it crosses a threshold (e.g. a subtle amber "12 unattended runs" chip near the schedule control) so a week of auto-firing can't accumulate slop invisibly. Server work is done (2026-07-03); this is UI-only, taste-profile rules apply.

Ideas worth revisiting. Add to this over time.

---

## Catmull-Rom waveform upgrade
The current `buildPath` function uses quadratic bezier (C1 continuity). Catmull-Rom gives C2 (curvature-continuous) which is visibly smoother on live CPU data. No new dependency needed — implement directly:
```
B1 = P1 + (P2 - P0) / 6
B2 = P2 - (P3 - P1) / 6
```
Generates SVG `C` commands instead of `Q`. Keep `useMemo` on the path. Drop-in replacement for `buildPath`.

## `@property --accent` for smooth ambient transitions
Using `document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--accent', color)` works but the color snaps hard. Register the property in CSS:
```css
@property --accent {
  syntax: '<color>';
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: #22d3ee;
}
```
Then add `transition: --accent 1.2s ease` to `:root`. Now the entire UI color-shifts smoothly as load rises/falls. Required for ambient color mode to feel premium rather than janky.

## Unified lower panel ("single instrument" layout)
Replace the 2-column card grid (RunHistory + ControlCluster as siblings) with one unified surface containing both as sections. Internal dividers = hairline `border-bottom` with `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)`. Removes the "dashboard of parts" feeling that the current floating cards create. Controls move to a horizontal icon row at the bottom, freeing vertical space for timeline.

## RunHistory as vertical timeline
Replace stacked cards with a vertical timeline: thin 1px left-edge accent line, circular color-coded nodes (cyan=CREATE, purple=MUTATE, green=RESEARCH), run content branching right. 24–32px between nodes. Looks intentional with 2 items; feels like a console event log with 4+. Ghost cards (opacity: 0.15, blur: 2px, pulsing) for the empty state — same card structure so no layout shift when real runs arrive.

## Cold instrument pattern — AI zone idle body
The idle compact mode body (`!loading && !analysis`) shows a text placeholder that has no structural relation to the loaded field rows. Apply the "cold instrument" pattern: render the same 5 FIELD_META rows with `—` values, labels at 50% opacity, same padding + hairline separators — identical DOM structure to the loaded state. Loading state is already this way. Idle should match. The reveal on first load then becomes a pure content swap with no layout shift. One block in `AnalysisBody`, compact branch.

## Offline header tint — AI zone
Three header states (idle / active / offline) currently look identical except the dot color. When `unavailable`, apply a red border-top tint (`rgba(248,113,113,0.15) solid 1px`) instead of `var(--border)` — mirrors how `intelligenceActive` shifts the border to accent. No new chrome, just the same pattern applied to the third state.

## Run status polling
After "Run Lab" is triggered, poll `/api/run/status` every 3s and show a progress indicator ("running…" → "complete"). Currently the feedback disappears after 800ms with no idea if the process finished. Would make the control feel real.

## narrator quality — temperature tuning
Run 63 audit (23 live samples, stale code): ~13% sensory. Garbled outputs ("arenaught", "areading") are tokenization artifacts from qwen2.5-instruct:1.5b — the model sometimes generates "I are..." as broken first-person. These are single-line so `.split('\n')[0]` doesn't catch them. After restart + quality assessment, if garbled rate stays high, consider adding `options: { stop: ['I are', '\n\n'] }` as a secondary stop signal. Primary fix is still temperature: 1.2 after restart confirms base quality.

## Day Ring + Machine Diary temporal linking — DONE (Run 50, 51)
Implemented in Run 50: DayRing hover cross-reference shows closest narration entry by timestamp. Run 51 added clock time label beneath the hover quote. Working. Gets richer as the ring fills to 12h+.

 # Backlog
 
+## Run parser should anchor stdout failure detection
+`parseStdoutRunBlocks()` currently uses `body.includes('[run failed')`, which means a successful Codex transcript can become `FAILED` if it quotes earlier log text or a diff containing that marker. Live evidence on 2026-07-03: `/api/runs` reported `FAILED #89` with the summary `[run completed successfully; verbose Codex transcript omitted...]`. Change detection to inspect the first meaningful stdout line, e.g. `lines[0]?.startsWith('[run failed')`, and keep quoted historical failures out of the status classifier.
+
 ## ghost/whisper/oracle as incubated project
 The quartet (src/ghost/) is dormant — 5 standalone JS files, ports 3032–3036. Per the seed, it must NOT be integrated into Pi Pulse's Pulse tab UI. The correct pattern: create `projects/ghost-trio/status.json` with repo/runLog/runScript fields, point `mounted.json` at it, restart pi-pulse. Then the quartet gets its own ProjectPanel slot and run history without touching the waveform layer. One status.json + one run script = fully mounted. This is the right way to continue the ghost/oracle work without violating the "no new instruments" rule.

+## Run 92 — 2026-07-03 — RESEARCH
+
+**What I investigated:** Pi Pulse incubator-host reliability around run parsing, API JSON boundaries, per-incubator local Ollama/Qwen feedback, and runner preflight behavior.
+**Key finding:** `parseStdoutRunBlocks()` treats any stdout body containing `[run failed` as failed; live `/api/runs` therefore reports a successful Codex stdout block for run 89 as `FAILED` because the transcript/log text contains that marker elsewhere.
+**Implication:** The next build run should tighten failure classification before adding more history UI, otherwise the timeline can confidently display false failures.

# Backlog

## Run parser should anchor stdout failure detection
`parseStdoutRunBlocks()` currently uses `body.includes('[run failed')`, which means a successful Codex transcript can become `FAILED` if it quotes earlier log text or a diff containing that marker. Live evidence on 2026-07-03: `/api/runs` reported `FAILED #89` with the summary `[run completed successfully; verbose Codex transcript omitted...]`. Change detection to inspect the first meaningful stdout line, e.g. `lines[0]?.startsWith('[run failed')`, and keep quoted historical failures out of the status classifier.

## ghost/whisper/oracle as incubated project
The quartet (src/ghost/) is dormant — 5 standalone JS files, ports 3032–3036. Per the seed, it must NOT be integrated into Pi Pulse's Pulse tab UI. The correct pattern: create `projects/ghost-trio/status.json` with repo/runLog/runScript fields, point `mounted.json` at it, restart pi-pulse. Then the quartet gets its own ProjectPanel slot and run history without touching the waveform layer. One status.json + one run script = fully mounted. This is the right way to continue the ghost/oracle work without violating the "no new instruments" rule.

## server.js: replace hardcoded 'race-whisperer-predict' fallback strings
`loadMountedProject()` in `server.js` has hardcoded fallback values (`name: 'race-whisperer-predict'`, `dir: '/home/admin/race-whisperer-predict'`, etc.) that fire when `mounted.json` is missing or malformed. The silent-catch was fixed on 2026-07-03 (now logs `console.error`), but the fallback still steers a broken config at race-whisperer. Better fallback: throw and let systemd surface it, OR fall back to a minimal safe stub that clearly identifies as a config-error state. Not urgent — the console.error already makes the failure visible.

## Surface auto-run staleness in ProjectPanel
`GET /api/child/schedule` now returns `autoRunsSinceHuman` — increments on every scheduled auto-fire, resets when a human triggers a run or edits the schedule. Surface it in ProjectPanel once it crosses a threshold (e.g. a subtle amber "12 unattended runs" chip near the schedule control) so a week of auto-firing can't accumulate slop invisibly. Server work is done (2026-07-03); this is UI-only, taste-profile rules apply.

Ideas worth revisiting. Add to this over time.

---

## Catmull-Rom waveform upgrade
The current `buildPath` function uses quadratic bezier (C1 continuity). Catmull-Rom gives C2 (curvature-continuous) which is visibly smoother on live CPU data. No new dependency needed — implement directly:
```
B1 = P1 + (P2 - P0) / 6
B2 = P2 - (P3 - P1) / 6
```
Generates SVG `C` commands instead of `Q`. Keep `useMemo` on the path. Drop-in replacement for `buildPath`.

## `@property --accent` for smooth ambient transitions
Using `document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--accent', color)` works but the color snaps hard. Register the property in CSS:
```css
@property --accent {
  syntax: '<color>';
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: #22d3ee;
}
```
Then add `transition: --accent 1.2s ease` to `:root`. Now the entire UI color-shifts smoothly as load rises/falls. Required for ambient color mode to feel premium rather than janky.

## Unified lower panel ("single instrument" layout)

+function readCpuTimes() {
+  try {
+    const stat = fs.readFileSync('/proc/stat', 'utf8')
+    const line = stat.split('\n')[0]
+    const parts = line.replace('cpu  ', '').trim().split(/\s+/).map(Number)
+    const [user, nice, system, idle, iowait, irq, softirq, steal] = parts
+    const total = user + nice + system + idle + (iowait || 0) + (irq || 0) + (softirq || 0) + (steal || 0)
+    return { total, idle: idle + (iowait || 0) }
+  } catch {
+    return null
+  }
+}
+
+function getCpuUsage() {
+  const curr = readCpuTimes()
+  if (!curr || !prevCpuTimes) {
+    prevCpuTimes = curr
+    return 0
+  }
+  const totalDiff = curr.total - prevCpuTimes.total
+  const idleDiff = curr.idle - prevCpuTimes.idle
+  prevCpuTimes = curr
+  if (totalDiff === 0) return 0
+  return Math.round(((totalDiff - idleDiff) / totalDiff) * 100)
+}
+
+function getMemInfo() {
+  try {
+    const mem = fs.readFileSync('/proc/meminfo', 'utf8')
+    const parse = (key) => {
+      const match = mem.match(new RegExp(`${key}:\\s+(\\d+)`))
+      return match ? parseInt(match[1]) * 1024 : 0
+    }
+    const total = parse('MemTotal')
+    const free = parse('MemFree')
+    const buffers = parse('Buffers')
+    const cached = parse('Cached')
+    const used = total - free - buffers - cached
+    return {
+      total,
+      used,
+      free: total - used,
+      percent: Math.round((used / total) * 100),
+    }
+  } catch {
+    const total = os.totalmem()
+    const free = os.freemem()
+    return { total, used: total - free, free, percent: Math.round(((total - free) / total) * 100) }
+  }
+}

+}

+}

+function formatUptime(seconds) {
+  const d = Math.floor(seconds / 86400)
+  const h = Math.floor((seconds % 86400) / 3600)
+  const m = Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60)
+  if (d > 0) return `${d}d ${h}h`
+  if (h > 0) return `${h}h ${m}m`
+  return `${m}m`
+}
+
+function getDiskInfo() {
+  try {
+    const out = execSync('df -B1 / 2>/dev/null', { timeout: 3000 }).toString().trim()
+    const lines = out.split('\n')
+    if (lines.length < 2) return null
+    const parts = lines[1].trim().split(/\s+/)
+    const total = parseInt(parts[1])
+    const used = parseInt(parts[2])
+    const pct = parseInt(parts[4])
+    return {
+      totalGB: (total / 1e9).toFixed(1),
+      usedGB: (used / 1e9).toFixed(1),
+      percent: isNaN(pct) ? 0 : pct,
+    }
+  } catch {
+    return null
+  }
+}

+function getNetworkRate() {
+  try {
+    const raw = fs.readFileSync('/proc/net/dev', 'utf8')
+    const lines = raw.trim().split('\n').slice(2)
+    const SKIP = /^(lo|docker|veth|br-|vmnet|virbr)/
+    let best = null
+    for (const line of lines) {
+      const colonIdx = line.indexOf(':')
+      if (colonIdx < 0) continue
+      const iface = line.slice(0, colonIdx).trim()
+      if (SKIP.test(iface)) continue
+      const fields = line.slice(colonIdx + 1).trim().split(/\s+/).map(Number)
+      const rx = fields[0]  // receive bytes
+      const tx = fields[8]  // transmit bytes
+      if (!best || rx > best.rx) best = { iface, rx, tx, ts: Date.now() }
+    }
+    if (!best) return { rx: 0, tx: 0, iface: 'unknown' }
+    if (!prevNetSample || best.iface !== prevNetSample.iface) {

+    const tx = dt > 0 ? Math.max(0, Math.round((best.tx - prevNetSample.tx) / dt)) : 0
+    prevNetSample = best
+    return { rx, tx, iface: best.iface }
+  } catch {
+    return { rx: 0, tx: 0, iface: 'unknown' }
+  }

+import { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react'

+
+const KEY_MAP = {
+  DIRECTION: ['direction', 'dir', 'duration', 'heading'],
+  STRONGEST: ['strongest', 'strong', 'best', 'winning'],
+  WEAKEST:   ['weakest', 'weak', 'worst', 'problem'],
+  DRIFT:     ['drift', 'drifting'],
+  NEXT:      ['next', 'mutate', 'suggested', 'suggestion', 'move', 'priority'],
+}
+
+function parseAnalysis(text) {
+  const fields = {}
+  const cleaned = text.replace(/\*\*/g, '').replace(/\r/g, '')
+  const re = /([A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*):\s*\n?([\s\S]*?)(?=\n[A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*:|$)/g
+  let m
+  while ((m = re.exec(cleaned)) !== null) {
+    const rawKey = m[1].trim().toLowerCase()
+    const value = m[2].trim().replace(/\n+/g, ' ')
+    if (!value) continue
+    for (const [canonical, aliases] of Object.entries(KEY_MAP)) {
+      if (aliases.some(a => rawKey.includes(a))) {
+        fields[canonical] = value
+        break
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  return fields
+}

+import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

+// Ambient color thresholds — shifts the whole UI accent as load rises
+const COOL   = { accent: '#22d3ee', dim: 'rgba(34,211,238,0.12)',  glow: 'rgba(34,211,238,0.35)'  }
+const WARM   = { accent: '#fb923c', dim: 'rgba(251,146,60,0.12)',  glow: 'rgba(251,146,60,0.35)'  }
+const HOT    = { accent: '#f87171', dim: 'rgba(248,113,113,0.12)', glow: 'rgba(248,113,113,0.35)' }
+
+function applyAccent({ accent, dim, glow }) {
+  const r = document.documentElement.style
+  r.setProperty('--accent', accent)
+  r.setProperty('--accent-dim', dim)
+  r.setProperty('--accent-glow', glow)
+}
+
+// Circadian ambient — bloom opacity and vertical position follow the time of day.
+// Night: dim and receded. Dawn: rising. Day: full presence. Dusk: fading.
+function useCircadian() {
+  const compute = () => {
+    const h = new Date().getHours() + new Date().getMinutes() / 60
+    if (h >= 22 || h < 5) return { opacity: 0.07, top: '-6vh' }   // deep night — receded
+    if (h < 8) {                                                    // dawn — rising
+      const p = (h - 5) / 3
+      return { opacity: 0.07 + p * 0.09, top: `${(-6 + p * 6).toFixed(1)}vh` }
+    }
+    if (h < 18) return { opacity: 0.16, top: '0vh' }               // day — full presence
+    const p = (h - 18) / 4                                         // dusk — fading
+    return { opacity: 0.16 - p * 0.09, top: `${(-p * 6).toFixed(1)}vh` }
+  }
+  const [state, setState] = useState(compute)
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const id = setInterval(() => setState(compute()), 60_000)
+    return () => clearInterval(id)
+  }, [])
+  return state
+}
+
+function fmtBytes(b) {
+  if (b == null) return '—'
+  if (b < 1024) return `${b} B/s`
+  if (b < 1024 * 1024) return `${(b / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB/s`
+  return `${(b / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1)} MB/s`
+}

+function parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, byNum, { legacyOffset = false } = {}) {
+  const stdoutRe = /^\s*<!--\s*stdout from (codex\s+)?run (\d+)\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})[^>]*-->([\s\S]*?)(?=^\s*<!--\s*stdout from (?:codex\s+)?run \d|^\s*## Run \d|$(?![\s\S]))/gm
+  let m
+  while ((m = stdoutRe.exec(content)) !== null) {
+    const [, codexMarker, slotStr, date, body] = m
+    const failed = body.includes('[run failed')
+    const boldRun = body.match(/\*\*Run (\d+)\s*(?:[—-]\s*([\w ]+?)\s*[—-]|\s*[—-]\s*done)/)
+    const num = boldRun ? parseInt(boldRun[1]) : parseInt(slotStr) + (!codexMarker && legacyOffset ? 1 : 0)
+    if (!num) continue
+
+    const rawType = boldRun?.[2]?.trim().toUpperCase() || ''
+    const type = failed ? 'FAILED' : ['MUTATE','RESEARCH','CREATE','RUN'].find(t => rawType.includes(t)) || rawType || 'RUN'
+    const lines = body.split('\n').map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean)
+    const failureLine = lines.find(l => l.startsWith('[run failed'))
+    const detailLine = lines.find(l =>
+      !l.startsWith('[run failed') &&
+      !l.startsWith('**Run') &&
+      !l.startsWith('---') &&
+      !l.startsWith('```')
+    )
+    const summary = failed
+      ? [failureLine, detailLine].filter(Boolean).join(' ')
+      : detailLine || ''
+
+    const existing = byNum.get(num)
+    const placeholder = existing?.type === 'RUN' && existing?.['What I changed'] === 'stdout captured with no summary'
+    if (!existing || (failed && placeholder)) {
+      byNum.set(num, { num, date, type, 'What I changed': summary || 'stdout captured with no summary' })
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+function parseFormalRunBlocks(content) {
+  const byNum = new Map()
+  const sections = content.split(/(?=^## Run \d)/m).filter(s => s.trimStart().startsWith('## Run'))
+  for (const block of sections) {
+    const lines = block.split('\n')
+    const header = lines[0].replace('## Run ', '').trim()
+    const parts = header.split(/\s+[—-]\s+/).map(s => s.trim())
+    const [num, date, type] = parts
+    const fields = {}
+    for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
+      if (line.startsWith('<!--')) break
+      const m = line.match(/^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.+)/)
+      if (m) fields[m[1]] = m[2]
+    }
+    const n = parseInt(num) || 0
+    if (n) byNum.set(n, { num: n, date, type, ...fields })
+  }
+  return byNum
+}
+
+function parseRunsFromLog(content, options = {}) {
+  const byNum = parseFormalRunBlocks(content)
+  parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, byNum, options)
+  return [...byNum.values()].sort((a, b) => a.num - b.num)
+}

+  { key: 'WEAKEST',   label: 'Weakest',   color: '#f97316' },

+function parseAnalysis(text) {
+  const fields = {}
+  const re = /([A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*):\s*\n?([\s\S]*?)(?=\n[A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*:|$)/g
+  let m
+  while ((m = re.exec(text.replace(/\*\*/g, '').replace(/\r/g, ''))) !== null) {
+    const key = m[1].trim().toUpperCase()
+    const val = m[2].trim().replace(/\n+/g, ' ')
+    if (val && AI_FIELD_META.some(f => f.key === key)) fields[key] = val
+  }
+  return fields
+}

+function AiStrip({ slotId, autoTrigger }) {

+      .then(d => {
+        if (d.ok && d.response) {
+          setAnalysis(parseAnalysis(d.response))
+          setLastRun(new Date(d.ts).toLocaleTimeString())

+      })
+      .catch(err => setError(err.message))
+  }, [slotId])
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (!slotId) return

+    } catch (err) {
+      setError(err.message)
+    } finally {
+      setLoading(false)
+    }

+// Simulated data for when the API isn't available (demo mode)
+function generateDemoStats(prev) {
+  const now = Date.now()
+  const cpu = Math.max(2, Math.min(95,
+    (prev?.cpu ?? 25) + (Math.random() - 0.45) * 12
+  ))
+  const memPercent = Math.max(20, Math.min(90,
+    (prev?.memory?.percent ?? 55) + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 3
+  ))
+  const totalMB = 4096
+  const usedMB = Math.round(totalMB * memPercent / 100)
+  return {
+    cpu: Math.round(cpu),
+    memory: {
+      percent: Math.round(memPercent),
+      totalMB,
+      usedMB,
+      freeMB: totalMB - usedMB,
+      total: totalMB * 1024 * 1024,
+      used: usedMB * 1024 * 1024,
+    },
+    temperature: 42 + Math.random() * 8,
+    uptime: (prev?.uptime ?? 86400) + 2,

+export function useSystemStats() {

+    es.onmessage = (e) => {

+        const data = JSON.parse(e.data)
+        prevRef.current = data
+        setStats(data)
+        setIsDemo(false)
+        setConnected(true)
+        if (demoIntervalRef.current) {
+          clearInterval(demoIntervalRef.current)
+          demoIntervalRef.current = null
+        }
+        setHistory(h => [...h, data.cpu].slice(-80))
+        if (data.temperature != null) {
+          setTempHistory(h => [...h, data.temperature].slice(-80))
+        }
+        if (data.net != null) {
+          setNetRxHistory(h => [...h, data.net.rx].slice(-80))

+## Run 89 — 2026-07-03 — MUTATE
+
+**What I changed:** Made selected-incubator AI feedback load from saved per-incubator state, added Core incubator feedback support, and forced unknown `/api/*` routes to return JSON 404s.
+**Why:** The seed called out stale/global AI feedback, misleading AI HAT+ labeling, card-switch-triggered regeneration, and API fallthroughs that produce `Unexpected token '<'`.
+**What improved:** Core now exposes its saved local Ollama/Qwen feedback through the same incubator strip as projects, switching cards no longer consumes an old trigger as a fresh analysis request, and bad API paths no longer fall through to `index.html`.
+**What broke:** Auto-analysis still keys off parsed run-list length, so repeated stdout blocks with the same parsed run number may not retrigger feedback.
+**Next move:** Track a stable per-incubator latest-run signature instead of list length so failed repeated runs and same-number stdout blocks can trigger one fresh local analysis.
+

+## Run 90 — 2026-07-03 — MUTATE
+
+**What I changed:** Preserved repeated stdout-only failed runs as distinct history records and keyed local AI feedback refreshes from the latest run signature instead of run-list length.
+**Why:** The seed called out failed stdout-only runs disappearing or showing empty summaries, and the active thread identified same-number failures collapsing before the incubator could explain them.
+**What improved:** The Core history now surfaces each repeated `codex exited 127` attempt as `FAILED` with the actual command error, and fixed-size histories can still trigger fresh per-incubator Qwen feedback when the latest run changes.
+**What broke:** The UI still displays repeated attempts with the same run number rather than a visible attempt suffix, so the distinct failures are separable by order and message but not yet labeled as attempt 1/2/3.
+**Next move:** Add runner/path preflight validation before enabling Codex scheduled runs so `codex: command not found` is caught before the loop spends a run.

+  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream')
+  res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-cache')
+  res.setHeader('Connection', 'keep-alive')
+  res.flushHeaders()
+  runClients.add(res)
+  const heartbeat = setInterval(() => {
+    try { res.write(':heartbeat\n\n') } catch { clearInterval(heartbeat) }
+  }, 25000)
+  req.on('close', () => {
+    runClients.delete(res)
+    clearInterval(heartbeat)
+  })
+})
+

+    res.status(404).send('Build not found. Run: npm run build')
+  }
+})

+    const failureLine = lines.find(l => l.startsWith('[run failed'))
+    const detailLine = lines.find(l =>
+      !l.startsWith('[run failed') &&
+      !l.startsWith('**Run') &&
+      !l.startsWith('---') &&
+      !l.startsWith('```')
+    )
+    const summary = failed
+      ? [failureLine, detailLine].filter(Boolean).join(' ')
+      : detailLine || ''
+
+    const formal = runs.find(r => r.num === num && r._source === 'formal')
+    if (formal && !failed) continue
+
+    const run = {
+      num,
+      date,
+      type,
+      'What I changed': summary || 'stdout captured with no summary',
+      _order: m.index,
+      _source: 'stdout',
+    }
+    run.signature = runSignature(run)
+    runs.push(run)
+  }
+}
+
+function parseFormalRunBlocks(content) {
+  const runs = []
+  const sections = content.split(/(?=^## Run \d)/m).filter(s => s.trimStart().startsWith('## Run'))
+  let searchFrom = 0
+  for (const block of sections) {
+    const order = content.indexOf(block, searchFrom)
+    if (order >= 0) searchFrom = order + block.length
+    const lines = block.split('\n')
+    const header = lines[0].replace('## Run ', '').trim()
+    const parts = header.split(/\s+[—-]\s+/).map(s => s.trim())
+    const [num, date, type] = parts
+    const fields = {}
+    for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
+      if (line.startsWith('<!--')) break
+      const m = line.match(/^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.+)/)
+      if (m) fields[m[1]] = m[2]
+    }
+    const n = parseInt(num) || 0
+    if (n) {
+      const run = { num: n, date, type, ...fields, _order: order >= 0 ? order : runs.length, _source: 'formal' }
+      run.signature = runSignature(run)
+      runs.push(run)
+    }
+  }
+  return runs
+}

+function parseRunsFromLog(content, options = {}) {
+  const runs = parseFormalRunBlocks(content)
+  parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, runs, options)
+  return runs
+    .sort((a, b) => (a._order ?? 0) - (b._order ?? 0))
+    .map(publicRun)

+const KEY_MAP = {
+  DIRECTION: ['direction', 'dir', 'duration', 'heading'],
+  STRONGEST: ['strongest', 'strong', 'best', 'winning'],
+  WEAKEST:   ['weakest', 'weak', 'worst', 'problem'],
+  DRIFT:     ['drift', 'drifting'],

+
+function parseAnalysis(text) {
+  const fields = {}
+  const cleaned = text.replace(/\*\*/g, '').replace(/\r/g, '')
+  const re = /([A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*):\s*\n?([\s\S]*?)(?=\n[A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*:|$)/g
+  let m
+  while ((m = re.exec(cleaned)) !== null) {
+    const rawKey = m[1].trim().toLowerCase()
+    const value = m[2].trim().replace(/\n+/g, ' ')
+    if (!value) continue
+    for (const [canonical, aliases] of Object.entries(KEY_MAP)) {
+      if (aliases.some(a => rawKey.includes(a))) {
+        fields[canonical] = value
+        break
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  return fields
+}

+const LOG_FIELD_COLOR = {

+}
+
+function parseRunLog(content) {
+  const blocks = content.split(/(?=^## Run \d)/m).filter(s => s.trimStart().startsWith('## Run'))
+  return blocks.map(block => {
+    // Strip stdout comment dumps
+    const clean = block.replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, '').replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n').trim()
+    const lines = clean.split('\n')
+    const header = lines[0].replace('## Run ', '')
+    const parts = header.split(' — ').map(s => s.trim())
+    const num = parts[0], date = parts[1], type = parts[2]
+    const fields = []
+    for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
+      const m = line.match(/^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.+)/)
+      if (m) fields.push({ label: m[1], value: m[2] })
+    }
+    return { num, date, type, fields }
+  }).reverse()
+}
+

+// ─── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+function fmtElapsed(secs) {
+  if (!secs || secs < 1) return ''
+  const m = Math.floor(secs / 60)
+  const s = secs % 60
+  return m > 0 ? `${m}m ${s}s` : `${s}s`
+}
+
+function fmtAgo(ts) {
+  const mins = Math.floor((Date.now() - ts) / 60000)
+  if (mins < 1) return 'just now'
+  if (mins === 1) return '1 min ago'
+  if (mins < 60) return `${mins} min ago`
+  return `${Math.floor(mins / 60)}h ago`
+}

+function parseStdoutRunBlocks(content, runs, { legacyOffset = false } = {}) {

+    const num = boldRun ? parseInt(boldRun[1]) : parseInt(slotStr) + (!codexMarker && legacyOffset ? 1 : 0)
+    if (!num) continue

 # Backlog
 
+## Run parser should anchor stdout failure detection
+`parseStdoutRunBlocks()` currently uses `body.includes('[run failed')`, which means a successful Codex transcript can become `FAILED` if it quotes earlier log text or a diff containing that marker. Live evidence on 2026-07-03: `/api/runs` reported `FAILED #89` with the summary `[run completed successfully; verbose Codex transcript omitted...]`. Change detection to inspect the first meaningful stdout line, e.g. `lines[0]?.startsWith('[run failed')`, and keep quoted historical failures out of the status classifier.
+
 ## ghost/whisper/oracle as incubated project
 The quartet (src/ghost/) is dormant — 5 standalone JS files, ports 3032–3036. Per the seed, it must NOT be integrated into Pi Pulse's Pulse tab UI. The correct pattern: create `projects/ghost-trio/status.json` with repo/runLog/runScript fields, point `mounted.json` at it, restart pi-pulse. Then the quartet gets its own ProjectPanel slot and run history without touching the waveform layer. One status.json + one run script = fully mounted. This is the right way to continue the ghost/oracle work without violating the "no new instruments" rule.

index e6ebad2b165dcee12593bd574bcebbe10d719eb0..80e61e0f6e03d511b83b53a0ef6d27894caf73e2
--- a/BACKLOG.md
+++ b/BACKLOG.md
@@ -1,5 +1,8 @@
 # Backlog
 
+## Run parser should anchor stdout failure detection
+`parseStdoutRunBlocks()` currently uses `body.includes('[run failed')`, which means a successful Codex transcript can become `FAILED` if it quotes earlier log text or a diff containing that marker. Live evidence on 2026-07-03: `/api/runs` reported `FAILED #89` with the summary `[run completed successfully; verbose Codex transcript omitted...]`. Change detection to inspect the first meaningful stdout line, e.g. `lines[0]?.startsWith('[run failed')`, and keep quoted historical failures out of the status classifier.
+
 ## ghost/whisper/oracle as incubated project
 The quartet (src/ghost/) is dormant — 5 standalone JS files, ports 3032–3036. Per the seed, it must NOT be integrated into Pi Pulse's Pulse tab UI. The correct pattern: create `projects/ghost-trio/status.json` with repo/runLog/runScript fields, point `mounted.json` at it, restart pi-pulse. Then the quartet gets its own ProjectPanel slot and run history without touching the waveform layer. One status.json + one run script = fully mounted. This is the right way to continue the ghost/oracle work without violating the "no new instruments" rule.

+## Run 92 — 2026-07-03 — RESEARCH
+
+**What I investigated:** Pi Pulse incubator-host reliability around run parsing, API JSON boundaries, per-incubator local Ollama/Qwen feedback, and runner preflight behavior.
+**Key finding:** `parseStdoutRunBlocks()` treats any stdout body containing `[run failed` as failed; live `/api/runs` therefore reports a successful Codex stdout block for run 89 as `FAILED` because the transcript/log text contains that marker elsewhere.
+**Implication:** The next build run should tighten failure classification before adding more history UI, otherwise the timeline can confidently display false failures.
+**Suggested next move:** Change stdout failure detection to anchor on the first meaningful stdout line, then verify `/api/runs` no longer reports `FAILED #89` for `[run completed successfully...]` while still preserving real `codex exited 127` failures.

+`parseStdoutRunBlocks()` currently uses `body.includes('[run failed')`, which means a successful Codex transcript can become `FAILED` if it quotes earlier log text or a diff containing that marker. Live evidence on 2026-07-03: `/api/runs` reported `FAILED #89` with the summary `[run completed successfully; verbose Codex transcript omitted...]`. Change detection to inspect the first meaningful stdout line, e.g. `lines[0]?.startsWith('[run failed')`, and keep quoted historical failures out of the status classifier.
+
 ## ghost/whisper/oracle as incubated project
 The quartet (src/ghost/) is dormant — 5 standalone JS files, ports 3032–3036. Per the seed, it must NOT be integrated into Pi Pulse's Pulse tab UI. The correct pattern: create `projects/ghost-trio/status.json` with repo/runLog/runScript fields, point `mounted.json` at it, restart pi-pulse. Then the quartet gets its own ProjectPanel slot and run history without touching the waveform layer. One status.json + one run script = fully mounted. This is the right way to continue the ghost/oracle work without violating the "no new instruments" rule.

+## Run 92 — 2026-07-03 — RESEARCH
+
+**What I investigated:** Pi Pulse incubator-host reliability around run parsing, API JSON boundaries, per-incubator local Ollama/Qwen feedback, and runner preflight behavior.
+**Key finding:** `parseStdoutRunBlocks()` treats any stdout body containing `[run failed` as failed; live `/api/runs` therefore reports a successful Codex stdout block for run 89 as `FAILED` because the transcript/log text contains that marker elsewhere.

+**Suggested next move:** Change stdout failure detection to anchor on the first meaningful stdout line, then verify `/api/runs` no longer reports `FAILED #89` for `[run completed successfully...]` while still preserving real `codex exited 127` failures.

+function readCpuTimes() {
+  try {
+    const stat = fs.readFileSync('/proc/stat', 'utf8')
+    const line = stat.split('\n')[0]
+    const parts = line.replace('cpu  ', '').trim().split(/\s+/).map(Number)
+    const [user, nice, system, idle, iowait, irq, softirq, steal] = parts
+    const total = user + nice + system + idle + (iowait || 0) + (irq || 0) + (softirq || 0) + (steal || 0)
+    return { total, idle: idle + (iowait || 0) }
+  } catch {
+    return null
+  }
+}
+
+function getCpuUsage() {
+  const curr = readCpuTimes()
+  if (!curr || !prevCpuTimes) {
+    prevCpuTimes = curr
+    return 0
+  }
+  const totalDiff = curr.total - prevCpuTimes.total
+  const idleDiff = curr.idle - prevCpuTimes.idle
+  prevCpuTimes = curr
+  if (totalDiff === 0) return 0
+  return Math.round(((totalDiff - idleDiff) / totalDiff) * 100)
+}
+
+function getMemInfo() {
+  try {
+    const mem = fs.readFileSync('/proc/meminfo', 'utf8')
+    const parse = (key) => {
+      const match = mem.match(new RegExp(`${key}:\\s+(\\d+)`))
+      return match ? parseInt(match[1]) * 1024 : 0
+    }
+    const total = parse('MemTotal')
+    const free = parse('MemFree')
+    const buffers = parse('Buffers')
+    const cached = parse('Cached')
+    const used = total - free - buffers - cached
+    return {
+      total,
+      used,
+      free: total - used,
+      percent: Math.round((used / total) * 100),
+    }
+  } catch {
+    const total = os.totalmem()
+    const free = os.freemem()
+    return { total, used: total - free, free, percent: Math.round(((total - free) / total) * 100) }
+  }
+}

+}

+}

+function formatUptime(seconds) {
+  const d = Math.floor(seconds / 86400)

+  const m = Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60)
+  if (d > 0) return `${d}d ${h}h`
+  if (h > 0) return `${h}h ${m}m`
+  return `${m}m`
+}
+
+function getDiskInfo() {
+  try {
+    const out = execSync('df -B1 / 2>/dev/null', { timeout: 3000 }).toString().trim()
+    const lines = out.split('\n')

+    const parts = lines[1].trim().split(/\s+/)
+    const total = parseInt(parts[1])
+    const used = parseInt(parts[2])
+    const pct = parseInt(parts[4])
+    return {
+      totalGB: (total / 1e9).toFixed(1),
+      usedGB: (used / 1e9).toFixed(1),
+      percent: isNaN(pct) ? 0 : pct,
+    }
+  } catch {
+    return null
+  }
+}

+function getNetworkRate() {
+  try {
+    const raw = fs.readFileSync('/proc/net/dev', 'utf8')
+    const lines = raw.trim().split('\n').slice(2)
+    const SKIP = /^(lo|docker|veth|br-|vmnet|virbr)/
+    let best = null
+    for (const line of lines) {
+      const colonIdx = line.indexOf(':')
+      if (colonIdx < 0) continue
+      const iface = line.slice(0, colonIdx).trim()
+      if (SKIP.test(iface)) continue
+      const fields = line.slice(colonIdx + 1).trim().split(/\s+/).map(Number)
+      const rx = fields[0]  // receive bytes
+      const tx = fields[8]  // transmit bytes
+      if (!best || rx > best.rx) best = { iface, rx, tx, ts: Date.now() }
+    }

+import { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react'

+
+const KEY_MAP = {
+  DIRECTION: ['direction', 'dir', 'duration', 'heading'],
+  STRONGEST: ['strongest', 'strong', 'best', 'winning'],
+  WEAKEST:   ['weakest', 'weak', 'worst', 'problem'],
+  DRIFT:     ['drift', 'drifting'],
+  NEXT:      ['next', 'mutate', 'suggested', 'suggestion', 'move', 'priority'],
+}
+
+function parseAnalysis(text) {
+  const fields = {}
+  const cleaned = text.replace(/\*\*/g, '').replace(/\r/g, '')
+  const re = /([A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*):\s*\n?([\s\S]*?)(?=\n[A-Z]{2,}[A-Z\s]*:|$)/g
+  let m
+  while ((m = re.exec(cleaned)) !== null) {
+    const rawKey = m[1].trim().toLowerCase()
+    const value = m[2].trim().replace(/\n+/g, ' ')
+    if (!value) continue
+    for (const [canonical, aliases] of Object.entries(KEY_MAP)) {
+      if (aliases.some(a => rawKey.includes(a))) {
+        fields[canonical] = value
+        break
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  return fields
+}

+// Ambient color thresholds — shifts the whole UI accent as load rises
+const COOL   = { accent: '#22d3ee', dim: 'rgba(34,211,238,0.12)',  glow: 'rgba(34,211,238,0.35)'  }
+const WARM   = { accent: '#fb923c', dim: 'rgba(251,146,60,0.12)',  glow: 'rgba(251,146,60,0.35)'  }
+const HOT    = { accent: '#f87171', dim: 'rgba(248,113,113,0.12)', glow: 'rgba(248,113,113,0.35)' }
+
+function applyAccent({ accent, dim, glow }) {
+  const r = document.documentElement.style
+  r.setProperty('--accent', accent)
+  r.setProperty('--accent-dim', dim)
+  r.setProperty('--accent-glow', glow)
+}
+
+// Circadian ambient — bloom opacity and vertical position follow the time of day.
+// Night: dim and receded. Dawn: rising. Day: full presence. Dusk: fading.
+function useCircadian() {
+  const compute = () => {
+    const h = new Date().getHours() + new Date().getMinutes() / 60
+    if (h >= 22 || h < 5) return { opacity: 0.07, top: '-6vh' }   // deep night — receded
+    if (h < 8) {                                                    // dawn — rising
+      const p = (h - 5) / 3
+      return { opacity: 0.07 + p * 0.09, top: `${(-6 + p * 6).toFixed(1)}vh` }
+    }
+    if (h < 18) return { opacity: 0.16, top: '0vh' }               // day — full presence
+    const p = (h - 18) / 4                                         // dusk — fading
+    return { opacity: 0.16 - p * 0.09, top: `${(-p * 6).toFixed(1)}vh` }
+  }
+  const [state, setState] = useState(compute)
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const id = setInterval(() => setState(compute()), 60_000)
+    return () => clearInterval(id)
+  }, [])
+  return state
+}
+
+function fmtBytes(b) {
+  if (b == null) return '—'
+  if (b < 1024) return `${b} B/s`
+  if (b < 1024 * 1024) return `${(b / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB/s`
+  return `${(b / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1)} MB/s`
+}
